QUESTION OF THE WEEK - Economists were again asked the probability of a cut in interest rates in November following Tuesday's Reserve Bank board meeting, or after the last meeting of the year on December 4. Last week, they saw a 60 percent chance of a November cut and, if no easing came, a 75 percent chance of one in December.
Employment Unemployment Participation Chance of cut

EMPLOYMENT - Employment is expected to have bounced a little in October following September's steeper than expected 34,100 fall but not by enough to bring the unemployment rate down from 8.7 percent. That level has already been cited by the Reserve Bank as too high, so such a result will further support the case for a monetary easing, assuming, that is, the bank has not
already cut rates on Wednesday after its November board meeting.

If the RBA does cut, the data may be useful in gauging the chance of another easing down the track, which analysts are starting to think is possible given the recent run of weak domestic data. A soft employment outcome and a jobless rate at the psychological 9 percent level would certainly stoke speculation the easing cycle might encompass more than one cut.

Bain revised down its forecast sharply Monday to -10,000/-20,000 from an original +20,000. The softness in September retail trade data and the fall of seasonal influences on the labour market suggest to us that we will not see a
rebound until November," Bain said on the revision.
A weak 1.0 percent fall in October ANZ job ads figures, released earlier today, might also lead to downward revisions in expectations, Bain said.
J.B.Were was the only other forecaster to follow as yet cutting its estimate to -5,000 from +5,000. The revisions took the median employment growth estimate to +12,000 from +13,000.
